before.html:
Question 1
?
Given that P(A)=0.55, P(B)=0.35, and P(A∩B)=0.15, find P(A′∩B′).
P(A′∩B′)=
Submit

decision.explanation: By De Morgan’s law and the addition law, P(A′ ∩ B′) = 1 − P(A ∪ B) = 1 − (0.55 + 0.35 − 0.15) = 0.25.

after.name: Question 1
after.worked_solution:
First, we calculate $P(A\cup B)$ using the addition law:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(A\cup B) & =P(A)+P(B)-P(A\cap B) \\  & =0.55+0.35-0.15 \\  & =0.75\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we construct the corresponding Venn diagram and shade the region ${A}^{′}\cap {B}^{′}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14041480/assets/e71239d41a4317c2c7c7015ee2947266075864cec768161fdc4874e8b48f5056.png)

Finally, we have

$$
P({A}^{′}\cap {B}^{′})=0.25.
$$

Question 3
?
Given that P(A)=0.5, P(A∩B)=0.2, and P(A∪B)=0.85, find P(A′∩B).
P(A′∩B)=
Submit

decision.explanation: A ∪ B consists of A and the disjoint B-only region A′ ∩ B. Thus P(A′ ∩ B) = P(A ∪ B) − P(A) = 0.85 − 0.5 = 0.35.

after.name: Question 3
after.worked_solution:
First, we calculate $P(B)$ using the addition law:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(A\cup B) & =P(A)+P(B)-P(A\cap B) \\ 0.85 & =0.5+P(B)-0.2 \\ P(B) & =0.85-0.5+0.2 \\ P(B) & =0.55\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we construct the corresponding Venn diagram and shade the region ${A}^{′}\cap B.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14041480/assets/43267ee39b162c12235739ea84e9be539015ea28627caf14828b5fb5cc9fcd7b.png)

Finally, we have

$$
P({A}^{′}\cap B)=0.35.
$$
